mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals economic weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate broad demand contraction, depressing corporate profit expectations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with both HOUST and RSAFS declining, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, rising federal funds rates increase equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production over 3 months signals weakening economic activity, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with INDPRO declining for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 800.0 thousand units signal housing sector contraction, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when HOUST < 800.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Weak employment growth combined with high unemployment (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.5%) indicates labor market deterioration, depressing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.5%, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong housing starts and retail sales signal economic peak, prompting profit-taking and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods identified as late-cycle expansion by high HOUST and RSAFS, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 5 years.
